note: Synthetic returns only. Real prices are never used here: a known-answer test must not change when the market does.

cases.name: two_identical_assets
cases.description: Two holdings with identical returns. Hand-derivable: ENB is exactly 1.

cases.name: two_independent_equal_vol
cases.description: Two independent, equally volatile holdings. Hand-derivable: ENB is exactly 2.

cases.name: pair_correlated_unequal_vol
cases.description: Two holdings, correlation near 0.6, one twice as volatile as the other.

cases.name: three_with_near_duplicate
cases.description: Three holdings where the first and third nearly duplicate each other.

cases.name: five_mixed
cases.description: Five holdings with uneven dollar weights, covering all four measures.

series_cases.name: returns_hand_derivable
series_cases.description: Closes a reader can divide in their head: +10%, -10%, flat, +25%.

series_cases.name: returns_sampled_300
series_cases.description: 300 sampled closes; checks the browser's arithmetic, not just its shape.

series_cases.name: basket_equal_weight_3_members
series_cases.description: Three members present every day; the basket is their daily average.

series_cases.name: basket_growing_4_members
series_cases.description: Four members, two of them listing on days 50 and 120. Before a member lists it is null and is left out of that day's average, not counted as a zero.

series_cases.name: rolling_correlation_window_3
series_cases.description: Window 3 over 6 days: 4 values, each covering the 3 days ending at it.

series_cases.name: rolling_correlation_window_126
series_cases.description: The registered 126-day window over 300 days, two series correlated near 0.55.

beta_cases.name: beta_portfolio_is_the_basket
beta_cases.description: A 50/50 portfolio of the basket's two members. Hand-derivable: beta is exactly 1.

beta_cases.name: beta_one_member_of_two
beta_cases.description: One of two independent, equally volatile members, held alone. Hand-derivable: beta is exactly 1.

beta_cases.name: beta_thirteen_member_basket
beta_cases.description: A 13-member equal-weight basket, as basket.json has, and four holdings: a member, a fund holding the members, an unrelated holding and one that moves against the basket.

replay_cases.name: replay_hand_derivable
replay_cases.description: One holding over three days: +10%, -50%, flat. $10,000 ends at $5,500.

replay_cases.name: replay_hold_or_rebalance
replay_cases.description: Two holdings, one doubling and one halving twice. Hand-derivable: held is $21,250 and rebalanced daily is $15,625.

replay_cases.name: replay_dips_and_recovers
replay_cases.description: One holding that falls 30% and comes most of the way back: the low is mid-window.

replay_cases.name: replay_five_holdings_60_days
replay_cases.description: Five holdings over 60 sampled days, unevenly split.

fall_share_cases.name: fall_share_passes
fall_share_cases.description: One day. The index halves; the portfolio is 60% in a holding that falls 30% and 40% in one that rises 10%, so it falls 14% against the index's 50% and its share is 0.28.

fall_share_cases.name: fall_share_at_the_threshold
fall_share_cases.description: The portfolio falls exactly half as much as the index - 25% against 50% - so the share is exactly 0.5 and level 6 refuses it: a portfolio that fell exactly half as much did not fall LESS than half as much. The boundary is a real build, not a limit.

fall_share_cases.name: fall_share_one_ulp_under_the_threshold
fall_share_cases.description: 20% against 40% is the same half as the case above in arithmetic, and not in binary floating point: 8000/10000 - 1 is -0.19999999999999996, so the share comes out at 0.4999999999999999 rather than at 0.5. Python and JavaScript land on the same bit, which is the point of carrying it. Both builds display as 0.5000 and both miss, because js/levels.js's passes() counts a measure within 1e-9 of its threshold as equal to it - the slack the star bands already give a guess. Without it, these two portfolios got different verdicts off the same number on screen.

fall_share_cases.name: fall_share_rose_while_the_index_fell
fall_share_cases.description: The portfolio gains 10% while the index falls 40%, so the share is negative. Rare but reachable, which is why level 6's lowest bucket has no floor.

fall_share_cases.name: fall_share_fell_harder_than_the_index
fall_share_cases.description: The portfolio falls twice as far as the index: a share of exactly 2.

fall_share_cases.name: fall_share_index_did_not_fall
fall_share_cases.description: The index ends above where it started, so there is no fall to take a share of and the answer is no number at all.

fall_share_cases.name: fall_share_four_holdings_23_days
fall_share_cases.description: Four holdings over 23 sampled days - the 2020 window's own length - unevenly split, against a sampled index. Checks the arithmetic rather than the shape: held dollars drift apart over 23 days, so this share is not the one a rebalanced portfolio would give.

puzzle_window.note: A game.json-shaped document and the correlation of each pair over the last 252 trading days both tickers cover. Synthetic; no real price is here.

cases.name: puzzle_window_AAA_BBB
cases.description: AAA and BBB over the last 252 trading days both cover, out of 300 in the file.

cases.name: puzzle_window_AAA_CCC
cases.description: AAA and CCC over the last 240 trading days both cover, out of 300 in the file.

cases.name: puzzle_window_BBB_CCC
cases.description: BBB and CCC over the last 240 trading days both cover, out of 300 in the file.

stress_window.note: A game.json-shaped document, the worst 10% of its index days inside the 756-day window, and both betas over them. Synthetic; no real price is here.

cases.name: stress_the_portfolio_the_game_is_named_after
cases.description: Three AI names, equally weighted - different tickers, one bet. The portfolio One Trade is named after, built by name rather than drawn.

cases.name: stress_is_the_basket
cases.description: The basket itself, equally weighted. Hand-derivable: the portfolio and the basket are the same series day for day, so beta is exactly 1 on ALL days and exactly 1 on the stress days too - subsetting cannot change an identity - and the loss is exactly the shock on the whole value.

cases.name: stress_mostly_quiet
cases.description: 80% in the quiet holding and 20% in one AI name: the case where the share of the money and the share of the risk come apart, and the beta is small.

cases.name: stress_hedged
cases.description: An AI name against the holding that moves the other way. Its two betas differ most, which is the instability the range is shown for.

cases.name: stress_window_cut_short_by_a_late_listing
cases.description: One holding listed 300 rows into an 800-row file, so the window is 500 days rather than 756 and the stress days are the worst 50 of those 500. The 10% is of the WINDOW, never of the file.

selection_cases.name: selection_ten_days_takes_one
selection_cases.description: 10 days, so floor(10 x 0.10) = 1 day - too few for a beta, which is an error, not a one-day beta.

selection_cases.name: selection_twenty_days
selection_cases.description: 20 days, so 2 stress days: the -0.07 on day 3 and the -0.06 on day 11.

selection_cases.name: selection_tie_at_the_cut
selection_cases.description: 30 days, so 3 stress days, and THREE days tie at -0.04 for the last two places. Ties break by date, so days 5 and 12 are in and day 26 is out.

selection_cases.name: selection_every_day_the_same
selection_cases.description: 40 flat days, so 4 stress days and nothing to choose between them. The first four by date are in - a rule, not a coincidence of the sort.
